solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Supplier of drugs quick to overcome injury

indicators.note: to overcome something is to get on top of it and envelop it, so one word wraps round the other

explanation.surface: A drug dealer moves fast to get past being hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supplier of drugs' sounds like a dealer, but it is a shop; 'quick' is an adjective for pace, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy is a chemist's shop that dispenses medicines to customers.

clue.text: Fork out megabucks for warheads, perhaps

parts.note: to fork out is to pay

explanation.surface: Someone pays huge sums for nuclear weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A missile's payload is the explosive charge it carries, so warheads are an example, flagged by 'perhaps'.

clue.text: A chap I restrained with great force

indicators.note: something restrained is held in, so one piece is kept inside another

explanation.surface: A man is held back by someone exerting real strength.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN holds I to make MAIN, after A. AMAIN is an old literary adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Amain is an archaic word meaning vigorously or at full speed, from 'main' as strength.

clue.text: Stoneworker's massive mother and male issue

parts.note: ma is a familiar name for mother
a son is male offspring, issue meaning children

explanation.surface: A stonemason's family described as huge mother and a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A monumental mason is a craftsman who carves gravestones and memorials from stone.

clue.text: Fall in pitch originally concerning gulf church

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the Gulf of Aden, off Yemen
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A fall in tone at first relating to a Middle Eastern gulf and a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadence is the falling modulation of the voice, as at the end of a sentence.

clue.text: Endless sea mist engulfing vehicle in foreign port

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is cut off
to engulf is to swallow up, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a haar is a cold sea fog on the east coast of Britain, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: Fog rolls in over a car in some port abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: HAAR is a Scottish and North-East English word for sea fog.
explanation.definitionFit: Havana is the capital and chief port of Cuba, a city abroad for a British solver.

clue.text: Completely finished, the fish, we hear — everywhere!

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: plaice is a flatfish, said like a word for a location

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the fish is done for and scattered everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for found in every location or widely scattered.

clue.text: I'd pass him irregularly in the centre of Sheffield, say

definitions.text: in the centre of Sheffield, say

indicators.note: irregularly means not in regular order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone passes a man now and then in central Sheffield, the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheffield looks like the Yorkshire city, but HMS Sheffield is a warship; 'say' signals the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidships means in the middle part of a vessel, and Sheffield has been the name of Royal Navy ships.

clue.text: Good health initially found in a supporter's dog

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the first letter of the word before is used

explanation.surface: A fan's dog turns out to be in fine fettle.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afghan hound is a tall long-haired breed of dog.

clue.text: Idiots consuming small bread rolls, possibly

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Fools eat small bread rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist is a loaf or roll of plaited dough, so bread rolls are an example.

clue.text: Long period of time before noon

parts.note: a year is a period of time
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A long stretch of time before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the period, but it is the verb meaning to desire.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something and to yearn for it are synonyms meaning to want intensely.

clue.text: Residence containing old carpenter's work

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A house with an old woodworker's handiwork in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowelling is joining wood with dowels, wooden pegs fitted into holes, a carpentry technique.

clue.text: Stern Mona trashed decorations

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A severe woman called Mona wrecked the decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornaments are decorative objects, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: View from pass crossing westmost part of Tyrol

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so one piece straddles another

parts.note: a visa is a travel pass

indicators.note: the westmost part of an across word is its left end, its first letter

explanation.surface: The view from a mountain pass across the western edge of the Tyrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' suggests an Alpine col, fitting the Tyrol, but here it is a travel document.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a pleasing view, especially a long narrow one.

clue.text: Poet inspiring the old senior member

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: A poet motivates the elderly to become a senior figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected or longest-serving woman in a group.

clue.text: Standard police department staff

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police headquarters
a staff is a walking stick

explanation.surface: The usual personnel of a police department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees; here it is a rod or stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard by which things are measured or judged.

clue.text: Sally's kind, extremely inventive

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the two end letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally is kind and very creative.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a woman's name, but a sally is a sudden charge out by troops; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie and a sally are both a sudden attack made from a besieged position.

clue.text: Most inspired lines about Iowa animal book

indicators.note: about means around, so the earlier pieces surround the next one

parts.note: the best is the most inspired
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of lines
IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa

explanation.surface: The finest verses on Iowa become a book about animals.
explanation.walkthrough: BEST and RY together go about IA, which drops in at their join.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestiary is a medieval book describing real and fabulous animals, often with moral lessons.

clue.text: Cook digesting broadcast about religious community

indicators.note: digesting means taking food inside, so one piece goes within another
about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A cook takes in a broadcast about a monastic community.
explanation.definitionFit: A friary is a convent or house of friars, a religious community.

clue.text: Fret over keeping a Eurasian plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards
keeping means holding, so one piece is held inside another

explanation.surface: Someone frets over holding on to a particular plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a strongly scented flowering herb, Achillea millefolium, native to Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Some made his cellar burst open

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of made, all of his and the start of cellar

explanation.surface: Something made a man's cellar explode.
explanation.definitionFit: To dehisce is a botanical term for a seed pod or fruit splitting open to release its contents.

clue.text: Noblewoman finally cooked high-class game

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A noblewoman at last served up some posh game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' suggests meat for the cooking, but it is a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess is a woman holding the rank of duke or married to a duke.

clue.text: Two graduates and bishop gathering round African tree

indicators.note: gathering means drawing together and enclosing, so the earlier pieces hold the next one

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Two graduates and a bishop collect around a tree in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: BA, BA and B together gather O, which slips in after the first BA.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is a huge thick-trunked tree of the African savanna.

clue.text: Tea served by a southern man or woman

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
Sam can be short for Samuel or Samantha

explanation.surface: Tea poured by a person from the South.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a strong black tea grown in the Indian state of that name.

clue.text: Stun factory, producing growth

parts.note: to rock someone is to stun them

explanation.surface: Shocking a factory into increased output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' reads as economic expansion, but it means something growing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock plant is one that grows among rocks, as in an alpine rock garden.

clue.text: Bitter as a native of Belgrade sounds?

indicators.note: sounds means what is said aloud matters, not the spelling

parts.note: a Serb comes from Serbia, whose capital is Belgrade

explanation.surface: A query whether someone from Belgrade seems sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare form of acerbic, meaning sour or harsh in taste or tone.

clue.text: Butterfly in seawater? Most unusual

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A butterfly in the sea would be very strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most unusual' reads as a comment on the scene, but 'Most' is the fodder and 'unusual' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The brimstone is a yellow butterfly common in Europe, named after sulphur.

clue.text: Tall palm found in a park area

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public park
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A tall palm tree growing in a park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' looks like a hidden-word signal, but the letters are not in the words; it only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca is a genus of tropical palm, including the betel-nut palm.

clue.text: British family touring island, primarily introducing swimwear

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the earlier pieces circle the next one

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
I is the abbreviation for island

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

explanation.surface: A British family on a tour of an island brings in a two-piece swimsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: B and KIN together tour I, which slips in at their join.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit for women.

clue.text: Convocation skilfully securing overthrow of disorderly state

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so one piece is held inside another
an overthrow turns something upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a mess is an untidy state

explanation.surface: A gathering cleverly brings about the overthrow of a chaotic regime.
explanation.definitionFit: A convocation is a formal gathering of people, and an assembly is a synonym.
